subject: Fitting a spatial temporal SPDE model when data is not available for all years

messages.author: 604c4e7a5e3606cc
messages.subject: Fitting a spatial temporal SPDE model when data is not available for all years
parts:
Hi,

I would like to seek advice whether it is possible to fit a spatial temporal SPDE model when the data is not available for some years. My analysis will be based on data that is available for the years 2000, 2004, 2010 and 2015-16 demographic health surveillance data.

If it is possible to do so? Will it also possible to predict for values on the years that did not have data?

Regards,
McEwen.

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Fitting a spatial temporal SPDE model when data is not available for all years
parts:
Hi McEwen,

yes, this is possible in principle. The details depend on what kind of
dependency model you want to have between the years.
You need to define your space-time model to include all the time
points that have observations as well as all the time points for which
you want to do prediction.
Whether those predictions are useful depends on how much information
there is about the temporal dependence in the data.

There are several options for spatio-temporal model; spatial field
plus spatially varying trend would be the simplest model, but could be
unrealistic.
A spatial model with an ar1 model as "group" model would be more flexible.
To make sure the model can be estimated, and since most of your data
is roughly equi-distant in time, I would suggest forst estimating the
model
using only the timepoints that have data (mapping 2000,2004,2010 and
2015 to 1, 2, 3, 4). That's less expensive to compute, and will show
if you have a model that at least fits the data you have, before
extending it to do interpolation/prediction.

Finn
